items.front: How is a queue implemented on a linked list, and what is the time complexity of its operations?
items.back: A queue can be built on a linked list with O(1) operations.

items.front: Why does a queue on a plain array need a circular buffer?
items.back: So that dequeue does not shift every element.

items.front: In a queue, what do enqueue and dequeue do?
items.back: Enqueue adds at the back and dequeue removes from the front.

items.front: How is a stack used to match brackets in an expression?
items.back: Push each opening bracket; on a closing bracket, pop and compare.

items.front: What do the push, pop, and peek operations of a stack do?
items.back: Push adds to the top, pop removes from the top, and peek reads the top without removing it.
